_comment: Your server information for DATA 6200. You get ONE app, ONE port and ONE
database for the whole course, so this is where they get written down once
and stay written down. Every value comes off the Deployments page in the
THIS FILE IS COMMITTED, and that is safe: every value in it is already
public. Your port is in your URL, your database name is in your logs.
THE DATABASE PASSWORD IS NOT IN HERE AND MUST NEVER BE ADDED. It goes two
places, neither of them a file git tracks: .env on your laptop (which
.gitignore blocks) and config:set on the server. That split is the whole
lesson of Database + SQL - the NAME of a secret lives in your code, the
VALUE lives somewhere the code can reach and the repository cannot.
Check your answers against the real server with:  python check_server.py
What a filled-in file looks like, for a student whose netid is
sam.rivers and whose port is 7210. Yours will have a different port.
Note how little of this you actually choose: the app name is your netid
with dots turned into dashes, the database name is the app name with
dashes turned into underscores, and the username is the database name.
Only the port is assigned to you.
